newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ailing Thai bank looks at two buy out offers.
newsitem.headline: Ailing Thai bank looks at two buy out offers.

text.p: Ailing Bangkok Bank of Commmerce Plc said on Thursday that Nithipat Capital Plc and SITCA Investment and Securities Plc would be invited to further talks on their offers for the bank's stock.
BBC Vice-President Viravudh Vajirabajr told Reuters that executives from the two local finance and securities companies had been asked to meet with the bank's governing control committee on Monday.
A third offer made by locally-incorporated Black Forrest Holding Corp had been rejected, he said.
"The committee has considered the report from the working committee on the three groups and has agreed on two points," he said.

"The first is the removal of Black Forrest from the list of prospective bidders, the second is to invite Nithipat and SITCA to come in on Monday morning to clarify and confirm their proposals," Viravudh added.
He noted Black Forrest's offer had been rejected since the group's sources of funding were unclear.
The government-appointed control committee handling BBC's affairs was appointed in May after the bank was discovered to have non-performing loans estimated at 70 billion baht.
The Thai government, currently the bank's majority shareholder, has offered BBC for sale.
Nithipat and Sitca have offered to buy 30 percent of the bank's 35 million shares at their 10-baht par value.
They plan to sell off the bank's non-performing loans to a subsidiary of the Bank of Thailand's Financial Institution's Rehabilitation Fund.

Black Forrest had offered to buy 40 percent of the bank's stock at 20 baht per share and said it would inject several billion dollars into the bank. The group had also proposed the setting up of a private company to handle the bank's debts.
